## 固定收益開盤主論

低於預期的整體通膨數據降低市場對聯準會近期升息的預期，美國公債殖利率曲線因而在6月25日收陡；但午後油價反彈，又讓較長天期債券重新納入部分通膨溢價。2年期殖利率下跌2.4個基點至4.124%，5年期下跌1.1個基點至4.166%；10年期幾乎持平於4.394%，30年期則上升2.1個基點至4.862%。這項分歧使2年期與10年期利差擴大2.5個基點至27個基點，2年期與30年期利差擴大4.5個基點至73.8個基點。

10年期殖利率的組成反映了兩股相反力量。5月個人消費支出（PCE）通膨未出現市場擔心的上行意外，10年期實質殖利率因而下跌2.1個基點至2.18%。但荷莫茲海峽一艘船遭不明飛行物擊中、數艘貨輪折返，原油也逆轉早盤跌勢，帶動10年期損益兩平通膨率上升2.2個基點至2.214%。WTI收漲2.25%至每桶$71.92，布蘭特原油在一度接近戰前水準後收漲2.06%至$75.26。

5月整體PCE價格月增0.4%，低於0.5%的預估中位數；核心價格則如預期上升0.3%。市場定價顯示，截至12月的升息幅度由36個基點降至約34個基點，7月升息的隱含機率也降至約三分之一。不過，就通膨水準而言，這份報告並不溫和：整體通膨年增率加速至4.1%，核心通膨升至3.4%，為2023年以來最高。

其他數據呈現景氣分歧但仍具韌性。初領失業救濟金人數降至21.5萬，續領人數卻升至182.1萬。運輸設備訂單大幅反轉，拖累耐久財訂單下降4.5%，但排除運輸的訂單增加1.3%。堪薩斯城聯準銀行製造業指數改善，價格指標則升至2022年以來最高。加上第1季經濟成長年率獲上修至2.1%，這些數據削弱立即升息的理由，卻也未提供足以讓聯準會放鬆整體升息傾向的持續性通膨降溫證據。

財政部標售$440億7年期公債，得標殖利率為4.260%，與投標截止前的市場水準一致，市場無須額外讓利便吸收本週最後一筆附息債供給。然而，航運風險重新傳導至油市後，長天期債券未能守住早盤漲幅。這次收盤與其說是市場判定通膨已見頂，不如說是重新定價通膨來源：實質殖利率下降反映市場對基礎通膨壓力稍感釋然，損益兩平通膨率上升則反映投資人仍為能源供給再度中斷保留保障。

## PCE緩解帶動實質殖利率下滑，但數據仍維持升息傾向

美國公債最初全面上漲。整體PCE價格月增0.4%，低於預期，帶動各天期殖利率降至至少一週低點；30年期殖利率一度觸及4.82%，為3月以來最低。不過，這僅是相對緩解，而非通膨水準已轉為溫和。整體通膨年增率升至4.1%，核心價格月增0.3%，使核心通膨年增率達3.4%。

這項區別在聯準會6月會議後格外重要，當時支持升息的官員範圍已經擴大。19名決策官員中有9人預測今年至少升息一次，主席Kevin Warsh強調物價穩定，也已推動2年期殖利率於6月22日升至4.23%的16個月高點。週四公布的數據降低聯準會因通膨結果更差而立即回應的風險，卻沒有推翻物價增幅仍遠高於2%目標的判斷。

芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee認為報告中部分內容帶來希望，但仍強調通膨過高。他尤其擔心核心指標，並表示其走勢正朝錯誤方向發展。即使整體月增率低於預期，Goolsbee仍把通膨再度升高視為聯準會目前面臨的首要問題，維持以通膨為重心的立場。

紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams的著眼點略有不同。他取消公開露面後發布預先準備的講稿，表示目前政策立場已妥善定位，可望恢復物價穩定。他認為通膨無疑仍偏高，主要來源包括關稅、伊朗相關能源衝擊及人工智慧投資熱潮。

Williams預期通膨將在年底前降至3.5%，之後逐步回落，至2028年達到2%。他認為關稅影響消退及住房通膨放緩應有助益；若中東衝突相對迅速地獲得解決，能源與商品價格也可能趨穩。不過，這項預測附帶重要條件：AI投資可能使價格升幅高於預期，戰爭造成的供給中斷則仍對成長與通膨構成風險。因此，這是有利假設下的緩慢通膨降溫路徑，並非放棄限制性政策的理由。

勞動市場證據同樣支持耐心觀察，而非迅速轉向。截至6月20日當週，初領失業救濟金人數由上修後的22.7萬減少1.2萬至21.5萬；但4週移動平均由修正後的22.35萬升至22.425萬。在前一統計週，領取失業保險人數增加2.1萬至182.1萬，4週平均增加9,000至179.45萬；投保失業率維持1.2%。

兩者背離顯示，雇主並未加速裁員，但已在領取救濟金的勞工需要更長時間才能停止領取。這與近期企業調查顯示的招聘疲弱相互呼應，但仍不足以證明就業情勢全面惡化。對聯準會而言，這項組合降低保護勞動市場的急迫性；失業期間延長也意味著，不能只看初領人數下降便下判斷。

5月耐久財訂單同樣呈現分歧。整體訂單在4月增幅上修至8.5%後，5月減少4.5%，即$156億，降至$3,321億。運輸設備訂單下降14%，即$185億，至$1,135億，降幅甚至超過整體訂單減量。排除運輸的訂單增加1.3%，排除國防的訂單則下降4.6%。

飛機訂單占比較高的反轉，使整體數字看起來比其餘耐久財需求更弱。由於排除國防的數字仍為負值，且完整工廠訂單報告要到7月2日才會公布，這不足以證明投資全面繁榮；但也顯示，不能把4.5%的降幅解讀為企業需求普遍萎縮。

地區製造業數據顯示活動轉強，但價格訊號較不令人安心。堪薩斯城聯準銀行月度綜合指數由4月的10、5月的8升至6月的11；生產、新訂單及就業均改善，兩項庫存指數則仍為負值。年增綜合指數由17降至15，未來6個月預期指數維持19。

對通膨辯論更重要的是，原物料及製成品價格指數均升至2022年以來最高。這份涵蓋106家工廠、於6月17日至22日進行的調查只是一項地區觀察，但顯示當前活動加速之際，上游成本及銷售價格壓力也再度升高，與單靠原油下跌便能順利讓通膨回到目標的看法並不相容。

本週公債上漲後，7年期標售顯示中期美國公債需求仍在。這筆$440億債券以4.260%得標，與下午1時投標截止前的指示殖利率一致。自標售公告以來，其指示殖利率一度高達4.40%；投資人到標售時已接受低得多的殖利率，仍未要求額外定價讓利。繼本週2年期及5年期供給獲穩健承接後，固定利率附息債標售將暫停，直到7月7日標售3年期公債。

較短天期國庫券也順利標售，未見融資壓力。財政部$750億56天期國庫券的最高得標利率為3.660%，投標倍數2.79倍；間接投標人取得獲接受競爭性投標的69.52%，直接投標人占2.62%，交易商占27.85%。$700億28天期國庫券的最高得標利率為3.610%，投標倍數2.74倍；間接投標人占65.14%，直接投標人占3.63%，交易商占31.23%。兩者均於6月30日交割。由於缺乏發行前交易參考，結果只能確認承接情況及投標人分布，無法判斷得標利率低於市場水準或出現尾差。

前一交易日上漲後，美國公債交易活動趨緩。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$1.237兆，較6月24日減少15.3%；名目附息債交易量下降14.5%至$9,501億。主要天期區段成交均減少，其中剩餘期限不超過2年的附息債下降33.9%，3年至5年區段減少11%，超過7年至10年區段下降12.2%。這些數字涵蓋雙向交易，但顯示殖利率曲線調整發生在現券成交量下降之際，並非又一個交易異常熱絡的時段。

## 荷莫茲干擾令長端再度反映能源風險

當日大部分時間，油價都在強化通膨降溫的敘事。隨著貨輪駛出波斯灣，買方也收到中東及非洲供應商的大量報價，布蘭特原油一度跌破戰前收盤價$72.48。實體供應改善已促使經濟學家下調對歐洲升息幅度的預估，也減輕能源進口經濟體面臨的一項最直接通膨威脅。

但一艘貨輪在阿曼東南方遭不明飛行物擊中，數艘船在試圖通過荷莫茲海峽時折返，使情勢出現變化。英國海事貿易行動辦公室通報船體受損，白宮則表示現在判定責任歸屬仍為時過早。油價轉漲，布蘭特盤中升破$75，最後收於$75.26；WTI收在接近$72。

這起事件並未抹去航道重啟的事實，也沒有逆轉原油一個月來的大跌。WTI一週仍下跌6.11%、一個月下跌25.55%；布蘭特同期分別下跌5.75%及27.31%。不過，事件證明船舶恢復通行並不代表中斷風險已經消除。美國公債殖利率曲線尾盤轉陡、10年期損益兩平通膨率上升，均符合這項區別。

外交條件仍未定案。美國國務卿Marco Rubio反對伊朗向通過海峽的船隻徵收任何通行費或其他費用，理由是這將為控制戰略水道的其他國家開創先例。阿曼也加入美國與海灣阿拉伯國家合作委員會的聲明，反對徵收通行費、其他費用或企圖主張控制權；但伊朗與阿曼先前曾討論共同管理航道及海事管理成本。

美國與伊朗預定下週在瑞士進一步談判。海灣國家也要求就伊朗飛彈、地區代理勢力及戰時損害賠償取得保證。依臨時安排，伊朗預計可獲得財務誘因，可能包括使用開發資金及凍結資產，但資金規模及獲准用途仍有爭議。這起航運事件使市場焦點從目前原油流量，重新轉向政治安排能否持久及落實。

能源價格反轉，解釋了PCE數據壓低實質殖利率之際，通膨補償為何反而上升。當投資人下調未來通膨預期時，傳統美國公債會受惠，TIPS卻不會同等受益於通膨補償下降。6月25日，10年期實質殖利率降至2.18%，但損益兩平通膨率上升，使名目10年期殖利率幾乎不變。30年期債券對通膨及期限溢價不確定性的曝險較大，表現因而落後前端。

歐洲利率面臨同樣的拉鋸。歐洲央行本月進行2023年以來首次升息後，Oxford Economics取消進一步升息預測，認為能源價格迅速下降已使最初的通膨升勢提早結束。Capital Economics也改為預測只升息一次。RBC Capital Markets預期9月還會最後升息一次；野村仍預測9月及12月升息，但已取消原先預估的2027年3月升息。

市場仍反映今年再升息25個基點。法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin表示，由於油價衝擊已開始向其他價格擴散，本月升息25個基點有其必要。他把這次升息形容為溫和之舉，並表示此舉展現歐洲央行防止通膨失控的決心。不過，他也承認油價已低於最新預測所採用的假設，並表示停火使法國轉向較有利的經濟情境。

能源成本下降已經支撐歐洲公債。英國公債全週上漲，報酬率升至3個月最高，10年期殖利率則降至約4.7%，為3月中以來最低。儘管首相Keir Starmer辭職後政治情勢不明，漲勢仍然延續，顯示油價帶來的通膨展望變化，影響大於市場對領導權交接的短期憂慮。

隨原油回落，印度利率展望也不再那麼不利。貨幣政策委員會委員Nagesh Kumar表示，若油價維持在每桶約$70，截至2027年3月的財政年度經濟成長率可能超過7%。若成真，將扭轉印度央行近期把成長預測下修至6.6%時所反映的部分謹慎看法。Kumar也預期印度央行在8月5日檢討時，會將5.1%的通膨預測下修至4%目標以內。

這項條件相當重要，因為印度約90%的石油仰賴進口。Kumar把近期通膨衝擊定性為成本推動壓力，而非需求過剩，並表示目前第二輪效應有限。國內主要限制來自季風：截至6月22日，累計降雨量較正常水準低43%；若短缺持續，農業產出及農村需求將面臨風險。

跨資產交易反映一項通膨風險減輕，但收盤並未呈現全面追逐風險。美光的預測重新提振市場對AI需求的信心，帶動那斯達克100指數上漲0.75%、半導體指數上漲3.59%；標普500指數仍幾乎持平於7,357.49。蘋果在調高Mac、iPad及家用裝置價格後下跌6.1%，抵銷大部分晶片股漲勢。為吸收記憶體及儲存成本飆升，該公司調價幅度為$100至$500，顯示AI投資熱潮不僅反映在資本支出，也已傳導至消費品價格。

美元指數下跌0.18%至101.43，但整月仍上漲2.12%。黃金期貨先前跌破$4,000後回升1.01%至$4,030.50，整月仍下跌10.85%。這些走勢符合近期聯準會升息風險小幅下降，而非強勢美元及較高實質利率環境全面逆轉。

## 日本超長天期標售凸顯財政與日本央行不確定性的代價

日本20年期公債標售需求為2025年5月市場動盪以來最弱。投標倍數降至2.97，不僅低於3，也遠低於過去12個月平均；標售尾差為1月以來最大，最低得標價格也低於標售前估值。

這是日本央行把政策利率調升至1%後首次超長天期公債標售；1%也是1995年以來最高利率。投資人在承接長天期債券時，必須衡量通膨、日圓疲弱及擴張性財政政策可能使長期殖利率居高不下的風險。近期油價下跌已使日本公債殖利率從5月高點回落，但標售顯示，面對更高的按市價評價及政策風險，目前殖利率水準仍不足以吸引強勁買盤。

壓力集中於超長天期債券。日本國內保險公司5月賣出長天期JGB，逆轉財政年度初的買盤，全球資產管理公司也已開始降低曝險。因此，即使全球公債上漲，疲弱的標售需求仍可能使JGB殖利率曲線轉陡，尤其是在政府未來融資需求不明之際。

首相高市早苗的投資戰略進一步升高這項不確定性。計畫擬在截至2040財政年度前，動員超過¥370兆、即$2.3兆的公私部門投資，涵蓋AI及半導體等領域。政府預測假設每年投入約¥10兆財政支出，並增發過渡性債券，但尚未說明整體計畫最終需要多少新增政府借款，也未交代所承諾的成長效益會多快顯現。

新的多年期預算架構預計下個財政年度啟動，以稅收、其他支出節省額及政府公債，為經濟安全、危機準備及戰略性成長計畫提供資金。特別重要的投資可能列入特別會計，先以過渡性債券融資，直到取得永久性財源。

此架構旨在降低日本對大型追加預算的依賴，並提高長期投資的可預測性，但也讓未來借款決策成為市場評估財政時更核心的因素。日本政府債務已超過經濟規模的兩倍，其他潛在承諾仍缺乏完整財源，包括調降食品消費稅率，以及把國防支出提高至GDP的2%以上。

日本央行同時發出利率尚未到達終點的訊號。審議委員田村直樹表示，他的基準情境是每隔數月升息25個基點，逐步朝接近2%的中性利率前進。他在6月升息決策中與其他委員一同投下贊成票，過去也曾持不同意見、主張採取更高利率。

田村表示，升息速度取決於通膨。若上行風險變得更可能發生，日本央行就應提高升息頻率或幅度來加快步調。不過，他稍後在記者會表示，目前並不認為有必要迅速或大幅升息。因此，他的訊息並非要求立即再升息，而是主張央行定期持續正常化，只有在通膨可能超越這條路徑時才加速。

日本央行估計中性利率介於1.1%至2.5%，目前新政策利率1%仍位於區間下緣。田村表示，朝中性利率移動可降低通膨超越2%目標的風險，同時也強調央行有義務與政府保持溝通；現任首相向來支持貨幣政策提供支撐。

進一步緊縮的理由並不僅限於油價或日圓疲弱。日本央行官員日益把AI相關出口視為抵禦進口成本上升的緩衝。日本5月出口物價指數年增11.7%，為1979年以來最大增幅；電氣與電子產品出口價格跳升23.9%，創1976年有資料以來最高。全球AI投資同時支撐半導體設備及材料的出口量與價格。

這項強勢降低了油價衝擊必然造成日本經濟活動明確下滑的疑慮，也使政策取捨更複雜。能源進口價格上升仍會傷害貿易條件，但出口定價及外部需求對企業收入與國內通膨的支撐，可能強於先前預測。

美國固定收益市場收盤後，東京通膨提供下一項日本政策訊號。6月排除生鮮食品的消費者物價指數年增1.6%，符合預測，也是8個月來首次加速。排除生鮮食品及能源的通膨率達1.9%，整體通膨率則為1.7%。

補貼結束後水費上漲，汽油補助則持續壓低能源價格。主要基礎通膨指標尚未顯示通膨已高於日本央行目標，但在能源成本下降之際仍然加速，因而維持進一步正常化的理由。6月30日的2年期及7月2日的10年期JGB標售，將檢驗需求疲弱是否仍集中在超長天期債券，或已擴散至對下一步政策決策最敏感的天期。

## 信用市場重新定價SpaceX與石油出口國風險

美國整體信用市場持穩，但個別發行人定價顯示市場仍有明顯區別。投資等級債券基金LQD上漲0.08%，HYG上漲0.04%，JNK上漲0.09%，新興市場債券基金EMB則幾乎持平。這些走勢並未顯示午後油價反轉或殖利率曲線轉陡引發普遍壓力。

SpaceX本週稍早首次發行$250億投資等級債券後，新債相對美國公債走弱。其10年期債券交易利差為157個基點，高於發行時的140個基點。投資人在發行之初便要求其相對同評等公司債提供溢酬，之後利差進一步擴大，更清楚區分市場對公司成長前景的熱情，以及債權人對其資金需求的憂慮。

SpaceX信用違約交換（CDS）也開始活躍交易。交易商報價顯示，5年期保障的中間價接近每年1.255個百分點；為$1,000萬本金投保，每年成本約$125,500。評等相近的英特爾，其保障成本約為0.64個百分點。這項比較顯示，評等相同並未轉化為相同的市場定價。

CDS讓投資人無須交易新發現券，即可對沖SpaceX曝險或表達信用觀點。即使公司進行融資前持有大量現金，初期CDS水準仍反映市場對其龐大投資計畫、未來現金消耗及仰賴資本市場的疑慮。債券利差擴大及CDS報價只是市場價格，並非公司出現付款問題的證據；但保障成本確實高於單看評等類別所暗示的水準。

原油吐回大部分戰爭溢價後，非洲石油出口國面臨另一種重新定價。剛果共和國美元債券整月下跌逾2%，在納入比較的開發中國家主權債中表現最弱。安哥拉、喀麥隆、加彭及奈及利亞債券也都下跌逾1%，同期新興市場平均上漲約0.5%。

安哥拉2048年到期債券殖利率較6月初歷史低點上升逾60個基點至9.94%。剛果2036年到期債券殖利率上升約66個基點至10.01%，奈及利亞2034年到期債券殖利率則增加33個基點至7.33%。戰爭先前推升油價及預期出口收入，這些發行人因而表現突出；近期走勢已逆轉部分優勢。

各國實體原油市場狀況也有差異。中國需求疲弱，使部分安哥拉原油等級價格跌至逾10年最低，剛果也面臨買盤有限的情況。由於Dangote煉油廠已成為大型國內買家，奈及利亞原油表現相對穩健。因此，油價下降雖然削弱共同支撐，各主權發行人的政策落實、財政計畫及市場融資能力，仍將決定最終調整幅度。

6月25日原油反彈中斷跌勢，但未恢復先前石油出口國的意外收益。信用市場走勢目前更適合解讀為獲利了結及有利貿易條件動能消退，而非廣泛主權融資危機。若荷莫茲海峽持續遭到攻擊或限制再起，部分壓力可能逆轉；若航道持久重啟，焦點則會回到債務負擔及外部融資需求。

日本地區銀行因另一項結構性因素增加債券融資：存款競爭。橫濱金融集團首度發行¥120億3年期優先債，定價為JGB加27個基點；在訂單約達發行額1.2倍後，規模由原定¥100億提高。滋賀銀行及靜岡金融集團正考慮於7月首次發債，規模分別為¥200億及¥600億。

截至2025財政年度末，地區銀行放款年增4.6%至¥269兆，存款僅增長1.9%至¥348兆。日本央行升息及網路銀行競爭，使存款融資的可靠度下降，在年輕客群流向都市及數位金融機構的地區尤其明顯。優先債的成本低於次順位資本工具，投資人基礎也更廣，但這項轉變同時使資本市場融資更經常成為地區銀行的資金來源。

中國介入主權債務重組，也為困境信用市場提出另一項問題。中國人民銀行副行長宣昌能呼籲建立機制，遏制他所稱債券持有人的惡意訴訟，並依二十國集團共同框架落實債權人之間的可比待遇。

眼前爭議涉及衣索比亞。該國$10億違約債券持有人在未能就投資人團體與由中國共同領導的官方債權人都能接受的條款達成協議後，已著手準備採取法律行動。宣昌能也呼籲制定更明確的優先債權人認定規則；尚比亞及迦納重組案中，部分機構曾主張其債權應免於承受損失。這項提議並未改變既有債券契約，卻凸顯私人執行權、雙邊債權人條件與加快主權債務處理之間仍未解決的衝突。

## 中國增設隔夜工具，監管機構挑戰虛高評等

中國人民銀行將於6月29日及30日進行隔夜逆回購操作，在以7天期逆回購利率為核心的架構中增設新天期。這項變動讓央行能以直接工具管理隔夜資金狀況，最終也可能支持政策基準轉向更接近其他主要央行使用的形式。

現行7天期利率為1.4%，自2025年5月以來未變。新的隔夜操作將採固定利率，但中國人民銀行並未預先公布利率。實際水準將決定首次操作主要只是流動性管理調整，或帶有寬鬆訊號。

渣打銀行的Becky Liu表示，若利率為1.25%或更低，實質上相當於降息。法國農業信貸銀行策略師Jeffrey Zhang預期利率為1.3%，接近銀行間隔夜回購利率平時的交易水準；他並預期中國人民銀行仍將以7天期操作為主，只利用隔夜工具平滑季節性資金壓力。

轉換不太可能立即完成。中國利率風險避險所用的大多數合約仍與7天期回購利率連結，該利率也是現行利率走廊及新設海外央行回購工具的錨。若迅速取代，將擾亂既有定價及避險慣例。

消息公布後，中國公債仍小幅上漲，10年期殖利率下跌1個基點至1.73%，為5個交易日來首次下降。市場反應顯示，隨經濟成長失去動能，隔夜基準未來可能讓央行更精準控制銀行融資，或增添另一條寬鬆管道。

中國人民銀行也要求國內評等公司檢討中國債券市場中評等最高的發行人占比異常偏高問題。監管機構要求業者重新評估涵蓋的借款人是否仍符合更新後的AAA標準。一項擬議指標是發行利差相對可比政府公債的水準；利差超過200個基點的發行人可能遭降評，但評等機構也會考量其他因素。

截至第1季末，中國逾6,000家債券發行人中有27%獲得AAA評等，另有32%獲評AA+。相較之下，美國流通公司債中，由三大國際評等機構任何一家給予AAA評等者不到1%。即使多年來企業違約不斷，如此高度集中的評等分布依然存在，限制了評等區分信用品質的效用。

減少AAA評等可能提高較弱企業的借款成本，並擴大國內信用定價差異。目前仍不清楚會有多少發行人受到影響，中國人民銀行也未公開提出時間表。不過，在部分困境借款人仍保有國內最高評等後，這項措施代表監管機構更具體地嘗試把評等與市場定價及違約風險連結起來。

中國也在測試離岸市場對主權債的需求。財政部開始推介最高€50億的歐元計價債券，分為5年期、8年期及12年期，初步定價指引分別為中間交換利率加15、22及33個基點。距離上一筆€40億發債吸引逾€1,000億需求僅7個月，這次擬議發行也遠早於中國通常進入歐元債市場的時點。

在歐洲央行可能進一步升息前選擇此時發行，是要利用歐洲市場良好的承接環境；但在最終定價及配售確定前，交易仍未完成。初步條件顯示，中國在中國人民銀行重塑國內貨幣市場操作、監管機構試圖改善信用區辨度之際，也正尋求多元化融資。

## 前瞻市場意義

最接近的考驗是6月26日美東時間10:00公布的密西根大學消費者調查終值，以及紐約聯準銀行多變量核心趨勢通膨指標。密西根大學初值顯示，消費者信心為48.9，未來1年通膨預期為4.6%，長期通膨預期為3.4%。數據修正將顯示，週四航運事件發生前的油價大跌是否已開始改變家庭預期；紐約聯準銀行指標則將檢驗基礎通膨是否符合Williams預測的緩降路徑。

日本3個月期國庫券標售預計於6月26日日本時間12:35左右進行，公告規模約¥4.1兆。更重要的利率部位考驗隨後登場：6月30日將標售約¥2.8兆2年期JGB，7月2日則標售約¥2.6兆新10年期公債。結果將顯示20年期標售需求疲弱是否僅限於財政及超長天期風險，或反映日本央行升息後，市場普遍不願增加JGB曝險。

日本5月勞動、零售銷售及工業生產數據將於6月30日公布，7月1日接續發布季度短觀調查。這些數據將檢驗日本央行的看法，即AI相關出口及企業定價能力能否抵銷部分能源進口拖累。強勁的投資計畫或價格預期將支持田村定期升息的主張；若國內需求較弱，即使央行仍有意推動正常化，也會支持較緩慢的路徑。

中國官方製造業、非製造業及綜合採購經理人指數將於6月30日公布，前值分別為50.0、50.1及50.5。中國人民銀行推出隔夜工具之際，這些數據將首次廣泛檢視6月經濟狀況，判斷先前引發更多刺激呼聲的放緩是否延續。

歐洲通膨及勞動數據將成為市場下調歐洲央行升息預測後的下一項考驗。西班牙CPI初值及歐盟執委會企業與消費者調查將於6月29日公布，德國失業及CPI初值則於6月30日出爐。關鍵在於能源價格下降是否足夠迅速地削弱更廣泛的通膨壓力，或Moulin所擔心的價格傳導仍會出現在各國數據中。

美國國庫券供給將在季底前增加。財政部6月29日將分別標售$920億13週期國庫券與$790億26週期國庫券，並於7月2日交割；6月30日再標售$800億6週期國庫券。這些規模均大於前一次同類標售。由於這段期間不再標售固定利率附息債，需求與交易商獲配比例將檢驗跨季資金承接能力。

美國經濟活動日程隨後逐步走向因假期縮短的7月2日交易時段。JOLTS職缺及經濟評議會消費者信心將於6月30日公布；7月1日接續發布ADP就業、製造業PMI終值、ISM製造業調查及營建支出。前一期ISM報告顯示，製造業指數為54.0、價格指數為82.1，就業指數則低於50，因此6月數據組成將影響聯準會如何權衡產出韌性及持續的投入成本壓力。

6月非農就業及每週初領失業救濟金人數將於7月2日美東時間08:30公布。5月非農就業增加17.2萬人，失業率為4.3%，平均時薪月增0.3%、年增3.4%。財政部將於11:30標售4週期及8週期國庫券，之後依SIFMA建議，市場於14:00提前收盤，迎接7月3日假期。縮短的交易時段意味著，市場用來消化勞動數據意外、荷莫茲海峽再受干擾或標售疲弱結果的時間更少。

overall_summary.headline: PCE低於預期、壓低實質殖利率，荷莫茲風險卻推升通膨補償，美國公債殖利率曲線轉陡
overall_summary.session_narrative:
5月整體PCE月增0.4%，低於0.5%的預估，先帶動美國公債全面上漲；但通膨壓力持續，加上午後油價反轉，使收盤表現分化。2年期殖利率下跌2.4個基點至4.124%，5年期下跌1.1個基點至4.166%；10年期幾乎持平於4.394%，30年期則上升2.1個基點至4.862%。10年期實質殖利率下降2.1個基點至2.18%，損益兩平通膨率卻上升2.2個基點至2.214%。

這項通膨緩解仍有重要限制：整體通膨年增率加速至4.1%，核心通膨升至3.4%，堪薩斯城聯準銀行價格指標也升至2022年以來最高。隨後，荷莫茲海峽附近一艘船遭不明飛行物擊中，推升原油並讓長端重新反映能源供給風險。即使$440億7年期公債標售無須讓利便順利完成，殖利率曲線仍然轉陡。

日本則發出另一項長天期債券警訊：在未來政府借款及日本央行進一步正常化均有不確定性之際，20年期公債標售需求降至2025年5月以來最弱。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries ended June 25 with a steeper curve after a below-forecast headline inflation reading lowered near-term Federal Reserve tightening expectations, only for an afternoon rebound in oil to return some inflation premium to longer maturities. The 2-year yield fell 2.4 basis points to 4.124% and the 5-year declined 1.1 basis points to 4.166%, while the 10-year was almost unchanged at 4.394% and the 30-year rose 2.1 basis points to 4.862%. The divergence steepened 2s10s by 2.5 basis points to 27 basis points and 2s30s by 4.5 basis points to 73.8 basis points.

The composition of the 10-year move captured the competing forces. The real yield fell 2.1 basis points to 2.18%, consistent with relief that May personal-consumption-expenditures inflation had not produced the feared upside surprise. The 10-year breakeven rose 2.2 basis points to 2.214%, however, as a projectile struck a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, several freighters turned back and crude reversed an earlier decline. WTI settled 2.25% higher at $71.92 and Brent rose 2.06% to $75.26 after having traded near prewar levels.

Headline PCE prices increased 0.4% in May, less than the 0.5% median estimate, while core prices rose 0.3% as expected. That was enough to reduce the amount of tightening priced through December to about 34 basis points from 36 basis points, and to lower the implied probability of a July increase to roughly one in three. It was not a benign inflation report in level terms: headline inflation accelerated to 4.1% from a year earlier and core inflation reached 3.4%, its highest since 2023.

Other data reinforced the economy’s mixed but resilient profile. Initial jobless claims fell to 215,000, while continuing claims rose to 1.821 million. Durable-goods orders dropped 4.5% because transportation orders reversed sharply, but orders excluding transportation increased 1.3%. The Kansas City Fed’s manufacturing index improved and its price gauges reached their highest levels since 2022. Together with an upward revision that put first-quarter growth at a 2.1% annualized pace, the releases weakened the case for an immediate increase without providing the sustained disinflation the Fed would need to relax its broader tightening bias.

A $44 billion 7-year Treasury auction cleared at 4.260%, in line with the yield prevailing immediately before the bidding deadline, allowing the market to absorb the final coupon sale of the week without a concession. Yet duration could not retain its early gains once shipping risk re-entered the oil market. The close was therefore less a verdict that inflation had peaked than a repricing of its sources: lower real yields reflected relief on underlying prices, while higher breakevens preserved protection against another interruption to energy supply.

## PCE Relief Lowers Real Yields, but the Data Preserve a Tightening Bias

The initial Treasury reaction was broad. The softer-than-expected 0.4% monthly increase in headline PCE prices sent yields across maturities to their lowest levels in at least a week, with the 30-year briefly touching 4.82%, its lowest since March. The relief was relative rather than absolute. Annual headline inflation rose to 4.1%, and the 0.3% monthly increase in core prices left the annual core rate at 3.4%.

That distinction mattered after the Fed’s June meeting broadened support for higher rates. Nine of 19 policymakers projected at least one increase this year, and Chair Kevin Warsh’s emphasis on price stability had already pushed the 2-year yield to a 16-month high of 4.23% on June 22. Thursday’s release reduced the risk of an immediate response to an even worse inflation outcome, but it did not reverse the conclusion that price growth remains far above the 2% objective.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee described parts of the report as hopeful while maintaining that inflation was still too high. His concern centered on the core measure, which he said was moving in the wrong direction. Goolsbee identified a renewed inflation surge as the Fed’s principal current problem, preserving his inflation-focused stance even after the monthly headline number undershot expectations.

New York Fed President John Williams offered a somewhat different emphasis. In prepared remarks released after he canceled an appearance, Williams said the current policy stance was well positioned to restore price stability. He called inflation unquestionably elevated and identified tariffs, the Iran-related energy shock and the artificial-intelligence investment boom as its major sources.

Williams expects inflation to ease to 3.5% by year-end and then follow a gradual path to 2% in 2028. He said fading tariff effects and slower shelter inflation should help, while energy and goods prices could stabilize if the Middle East conflict is resolved relatively soon. The qualifications were material: AI investment may push prices higher than expected, and supply disruptions from the war remain risks to both growth and inflation. His forecast therefore described a slow disinflation path under favorable assumptions, not a reason to abandon restrictive settings.

Labor-market evidence also argued for patience rather than a rapid change of direction. Initial unemployment claims fell 12,000 to 215,000 in the week ended June 20, from an upwardly revised 227,000. The 4-week average nevertheless rose to 224,250 from a revised 223,500. In the preceding reporting week, insured unemployment increased 21,000 to 1.821 million, and its 4-week average rose 9,000 to 1.7945 million. The insured-unemployment rate held at 1.2%.

The divergence suggests employers are not accelerating layoffs, but workers already receiving benefits are taking longer to leave the rolls. It complements recent business surveys that showed weakness in hiring without establishing a broad deterioration in employment. For the Fed, that combination reduces the urgency of protecting the labor market while leaving the persistence of unemployment duration as a reason not to treat the lower initial-claims figure in isolation.

May durable-goods orders presented a similarly divided picture. Headline orders fell 4.5%, or $15.6 billion, to $332.1 billion after an upwardly revised 8.5% increase in April. Transportation-equipment orders accounted for more than the overall decline, falling 14%, or $18.5 billion, to $113.5 billion. Orders excluding transportation rose 1.3%, whereas orders excluding defense fell 4.6%.

The aircraft-heavy reversal made the headline look weaker than underlying demand across the rest of the durable-goods complex. It did not establish an unqualified investment boom, because the defense exclusion was negative and the full factory report remains due on July 2. It did show that the 4.5% decline cannot be read as a uniform contraction in business demand.

Regional manufacturing added firmer activity and less comfortable price evidence. The Kansas City Fed’s monthly composite rose to 11 in June from 8 in May and 10 in April. Production, new orders and employment all improved, although both inventory indexes remained negative. The year-over-year composite eased to 15 from 17, while the 6-month expectation held at 19.

More consequential for the inflation debate, both raw-material and finished-goods price indexes reached their highest levels since 2022. The survey of 106 plants, conducted June 17-22, was only one regional observation, but it showed that faster current activity was accompanied by renewed pipeline and selling-price pressure. That sits uneasily beside the proposition that lower crude alone will deliver a clean return to target.

The 7-year auction demonstrated continued demand for intermediate Treasuries after the week’s rally. The $44 billion issue was awarded at 4.260%, the level indicated immediately before the 1 p.m. deadline. Since the sale was announced, its indicated yield had been as high as 4.40%, so investors accepted substantially less yield by auction time without forcing a pricing concession. The result followed firm absorption of the week’s 2- and 5-year supply and begins a hiatus in fixed-rate coupon auctions until the July 7 sale of 3-year notes.

Shorter bills also cleared without evidence of funding stress. Treasury’s $75 billion 56-day auction stopped at a 3.660% high rate with a 2.79 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders took 69.52% of accepted competitive tenders, direct bidders 2.62% and dealers 27.85%. The $70 billion 28-day sale stopped at 3.610% with a 2.74 ratio; indirect bidders received 65.14%, direct bidders 3.63% and dealers 31.23%. Both issues settle June 30. Without when-issued references, the results establish absorption and bidder distribution but not whether either auction priced through or tailed prevailing levels.

Treasury trading activity moderated after the previous session’s rally. FINRA recorded $1.237 trillion of par activity, 15.3% less than on June 24, while nominal-coupon activity declined 14.5% to $950.1 billion. Turnover fell across the principal maturity sectors, including a 33.9% drop in coupons with no more than 2 years remaining and declines of 11% in the 3- to 5-year area and 12.2% beyond 7 and through 10 years. The figures describe two-way activity, but they show that the curve adjustment occurred on less cash-market turnover rather than another unusually heavy session.

## Hormuz Disruption Restores Energy Risk to the Long End

Oil had spent much of the day reinforcing the disinflation narrative. Brent fell below its prewar closing price of $72.48 as cargoes emerged from the Persian Gulf and buyers received abundant offers from Middle Eastern and African suppliers. The physical improvement had already encouraged economists to scale back expected rate increases in Europe and reduced one of the most immediate inflation threats facing energy-importing economies.

That story changed when a cargo vessel was hit by an unknown projectile southeast of Oman and several ships turned back while trying to cross the Strait of Hormuz. U.K. Maritime Trade Operations reported damage to the vessel, while the White House said it was too early to determine responsibility. Oil turned higher, with Brent trading above $75 during the session before settling at $75.26 and WTI finishing near $72.

The incident did not erase the reopening of the waterway or the month-long collapse in crude. WTI remained 6.11% lower over the week and 25.55% lower over the month, while Brent was down 5.75% and 27.31% over those periods. It did demonstrate that the return of visible shipping traffic had not eliminated the risk of interruption. The late steepening in Treasuries and rise in 10-year breakevens were consistent with that distinction.

Diplomatic terms remain unsettled. Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected any Iranian toll or fee on traffic through the strait, arguing that such a condition would create a precedent for other countries controlling strategic waterways. Oman joined a U.S.-Gulf Cooperation Council statement rejecting tolls, fees or attempts to assert control, but Iran and Oman had earlier discussed jointly administering the route and the costs of maritime management.

Further U.S.-Iran talks are due in Switzerland next week. Gulf states are also seeking assurances over Iran’s missiles, regional proxies and compensation for wartime damage. Iran is expected to receive financial incentives under the interim arrangement, potentially including access to development funding and frozen assets, but the permitted use and size of those funds remain disputed. The shipping incident returned attention from the volume of current oil flows to the durability and enforceability of the political settlement.

The energy reversal explains why inflation compensation rose even though the PCE release lowered real yields. Conventional Treasuries benefit when investors mark down prospective inflation, while TIPS do not receive the same boost from lower inflation compensation. On June 25, the 10-year real yield fell to 2.18%, but the breakeven increase left the nominal 10-year yield almost unchanged. The 30-year, which carries greater exposure to inflation and term-premium uncertainty, underperformed the front end.

European rates face the same tension. Oxford Economics abandoned its forecast for additional ECB increases after this month’s first hike since 2023, arguing that the rapid fall in energy prices had cut short the initial inflation surge. Capital Economics also shifted to a one-and-done call. RBC Capital Markets expects one final increase in September, while Nomura still anticipates moves in September and December but removed a previously expected increase in March 2027.

Markets continued to price one additional quarter-point increase this year. Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said this month’s 25-basis-point move was warranted because the oil shock had begun to spread to other prices. He described the increase as moderate and said it demonstrated the ECB’s determination to prevent inflation from escaping control. At the same time, he acknowledged that oil had fallen below the assumptions used in the latest forecast and said the ceasefire shifted France toward a more favorable economic scenario.

The decline in energy costs has already supported European duration. U.K. government-bond returns reached their highest level in 3 months after gilts rose throughout the week, and the 10-year yield fell to around 4.7%, its lowest since mid-March. The rally persisted despite political uncertainty following Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s resignation, showing that the oil-driven change in the inflation outlook outweighed immediate concern over the leadership transition.

India’s rate outlook also became less threatening as crude retreated. Monetary-policy committee member Nagesh Kumar said growth could exceed 7% in the fiscal year through March 2027 if oil remains around $70 a barrel. That would reverse some of the caution behind the Reserve Bank of India’s recent reduction of its growth forecast to 6.6%. Kumar also expects the RBI to revise its 5.1% inflation forecast lower and within the 4% target at its August 5 review.

The condition matters because India imports about 90% of its oil. Kumar characterized the recent inflation shock as cost-push pressure rather than excess demand and said second-round effects had so far been muted. The main domestic qualification is the monsoon: cumulative rainfall was 43% below normal as of June 22, leaving agricultural output and rural demand exposed if the shortfall persists.

Cross-asset trading reflected relief from one inflation risk without a generalized risk-on close. The S&P 500 finished almost unchanged at 7,357.49, even though the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.75% and the semiconductor index rose 3.59% after Micron’s forecast revived confidence in AI demand. Apple’s 6.1% decline after price increases on Macs, iPads and home devices offset much of the chip rally. The company raised prices by $100 to $500 to absorb soaring memory and storage costs, making the AI investment boom visible in consumer-goods pricing as well as capital spending.

The dollar index slipped 0.18% to 101.43 but remained 2.12% higher over the month. Gold futures rose 1.01% to $4,030.50 after their earlier break below $4,000, though they were still down 10.85% over the month. Those moves were consistent with a modest reduction in immediate Fed-hike risk, not a wholesale reversal of the stronger-dollar and higher-real-rate regime.

## Japan’s Super-Long Auction Exposes the Cost of Fiscal and BOJ Uncertainty

Japan’s 20-year government-bond auction drew the weakest demand since the market disruption of May 2025. The bid-to-cover ratio fell to 2.97, below 3 and well below its 12-month average. The sale also produced the widest tail since January, and the lowest accepted price was below the pre-auction estimate.

The result was the first super-long auction since the BOJ raised its policy rate to 1%, the highest level since 1995. Investors were being asked to absorb duration while weighing the risk that inflation, yen weakness and expansive fiscal policy will keep long yields elevated. Recent declines in oil had lowered Japanese yields from their May peaks, but the auction showed that those levels were not sufficient to generate strong demand from buyers facing greater mark-to-market and policy risk.

The pressure is concentrated in super-long maturities. Domestic insurers sold long-dated JGBs in May, reversing their buying at the start of the fiscal year, while global asset managers have begun reducing exposure. Weak auction demand can therefore steepen the curve even if global Treasuries rally, especially when the government’s prospective financing needs are uncertain.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s investment strategy intensified that uncertainty. The plan seeks to mobilize more than ¥370 trillion, or $2.3 trillion, of public and private investment through fiscal 2040 in fields including AI and semiconductors. Government projections assume roughly ¥10 trillion of annual fiscal spending and additional issuance of bridging bonds, but they have not yet specified how much of the program will ultimately require new government borrowing or how quickly the promised growth benefits will appear.

A new multi-year budget framework is expected to begin next fiscal year. It will finance economic security, crisis preparedness and strategic growth projects using tax revenue, savings from other spending and government bonds. Particularly important investments may be placed in special accounts and funded initially with bridging bonds until permanent revenue sources are secured.

The framework is intended to reduce Japan’s reliance on large supplementary budgets and make long-term investment more predictable. It also brings future borrowing decisions closer to the center of the market’s fiscal assessment. Japan’s government debt already exceeds twice the size of the economy, and other potential commitments—including a lower sales-tax rate on food and defense spending above 2% of GDP—remain incompletely financed.

The BOJ is simultaneously signaling that rates have not reached their endpoint. Board member Naoki Tamura said his baseline is a series of quarter-point increases every few months toward a neutral rate near 2%. He voted with the board for the June increase and has previously dissented in favor of higher rates.

Tamura made the pace conditional on inflation. If upside risks become more likely, he said the BOJ should accelerate by increasing the frequency or size of moves. At a later press conference, however, he said he did not currently see a need for rapid or larger increases. His message was therefore more specific than an immediate call for another move: the bank should continue normalizing at regular intervals and quicken only if inflation threatens to outrun that path.

The BOJ estimates neutral at 1.1%-2.5%, leaving the new 1% policy rate at the bottom of its range. Tamura said moving toward neutral would reduce the risk of overshooting the 2% inflation target, while emphasizing the bank’s obligation to maintain communication with a government whose prime minister has historically favored monetary support.

The case for further tightening is not limited to oil or the weak yen. BOJ officials increasingly view AI-related exports as a buffer against higher import costs. Japan’s export-price index rose 11.7% from a year earlier in May, the largest increase since 1979, while export prices for electrical and electronic products jumped 23.9%, the most in data going back to 1976. Semiconductor equipment and materials have gained both volume and pricing support from global AI investment.

That strength reduces concern that an oil shock must produce an unambiguous decline in Japanese activity. It also complicates the policy trade-off: higher energy imports still damage the terms of trade, but export pricing and external demand may sustain corporate income and domestic inflation more than earlier forecasts assumed.

After the U.S. fixed-income close, Tokyo inflation supplied the next Japanese policy signal. The consumer-price index excluding fresh food rose 1.6% from a year earlier in June, in line with forecasts and accelerating for the first time in 8 months. Inflation excluding both fresh food and energy reached 1.9%, while the overall rate was 1.7%.

Water-service fees increased after subsidies ended, while gasoline support continued to depress energy prices. The result did not show inflation already above the BOJ’s target on the principal underlying gauges, but it preserved the case for further normalization by showing a pickup despite lower energy costs. The June 30 2-year and July 2 10-year JGB auctions will test whether demand weakness remains concentrated in super-long bonds or spreads toward the maturities most exposed to the next policy decisions.

## Credit Markets Reprice SpaceX and Oil-Exporter Risk

Broad U.S. credit markets were steady, but issuer-level pricing showed meaningful discrimination. The LQD investment-grade fund rose 0.08%, HYG gained 0.04% and JNK added 0.09%, while the EMB emerging-market debt fund was almost unchanged. Those moves did not indicate generalized stress from the afternoon oil reversal or the curve steepening.

SpaceX’s newly issued bonds weakened relative to Treasuries after its $25 billion investment-grade debut earlier in the week. The company’s 10-year notes traded at a spread of 157 basis points, compared with 140 basis points when they were sold. The widening came after investors had already required a premium over similarly rated corporate debt at issuance, extending the distinction between enthusiasm for the company’s growth prospects and creditor concern over its capital requirements.

Credit-default swaps tied to SpaceX also began active trading. Dealer indications put the midpoint for 5-year protection near 1.255 percentage points annually, equivalent to about $125,500 a year for $10 million of insured principal. Protection on Intel, which carries similar ratings, cost roughly 0.64 percentage point. The comparison shows that ratings equivalence has not translated into equivalent market pricing.

The CDS market gives investors a way to hedge SpaceX exposure or express a credit view without trading the new cash bonds. Its early levels reflect uncertainty over the company’s heavy investment program, prospective cash burn and reliance on capital markets even though it entered the financing with substantial cash. The bond widening and CDS indications are market prices, not evidence of a payment problem, but they establish a higher cost of protection than the rating category alone would suggest.

African oil exporters faced a different repricing as crude surrendered most of its wartime premium. Republic of Congo dollar bonds lost more than 2% during the month, the weakest performance among the developing-country sovereign debt tracked in the comparison. Bonds from Angola, Cameroon, Gabon and Nigeria also lost more than 1%, against an average emerging-market gain of about 0.5%.

Angola’s 2048 bond yield rose more than 60 basis points from an early-June record low to 9.94%. The yield on Congo’s 2036 notes climbed about 66 basis points to 10.01%, while Nigeria’s 2034 yield increased 33 basis points to 7.33%. The moves reversed part of the outperformance those issuers enjoyed when the war lifted crude prices and prospective export revenue.

Physical-market differences matter within the group. Weak Chinese demand pushed some Angolan grades to their lowest prices in more than a decade, and Congo also encountered limited buying interest. Nigerian crude held up better because the Dangote refinery has become a large domestic buyer. Lower oil therefore removes a common support while leaving each sovereign’s policy execution, fiscal plan and market access to determine the eventual scale of the adjustment.

The June 25 rebound in crude interrupted the price decline but did not restore the earlier oil-export windfall. The credit move is still better understood as profit-taking and a loss of favorable terms-of-trade momentum than as a broad sovereign funding crisis. Continued attacks or renewed restrictions in Hormuz would reverse part of that pressure; a durable reopening would return attention to debt burdens and external financing needs.

Japan’s regional banks are increasing bond funding for another structural reason: competition for deposits. Yokohama Financial Group priced its inaugural ¥12 billion 3-year senior note at 27 basis points over JGBs, raising the size from an initially planned ¥10 billion after orders reached about 1.2 times the issue. Shiga Bank and Shizuoka Financial Group are considering debut sales of ¥20 billion and ¥60 billion in July.

Regional-bank loans rose 4.6% from a year earlier to ¥269 trillion at the end of fiscal 2025, while deposits increased only 1.9% to ¥348 trillion. Higher BOJ rates and competition from online banks are making deposit funding less assured, especially in areas losing younger customers to urban and digital institutions. Senior debt offers lower costs and a broader buyer base than subordinated capital instruments, but the shift also makes market access a more regular component of regional lenders’ funding.

China’s intervention in sovereign restructurings raised a separate question for distressed credit. PBOC Deputy Governor Xuan Changneng called for mechanisms to curb what he described as malicious litigation by bondholders and to enforce comparable treatment among creditors under the Group of 20 Common Framework.

The immediate dispute concerns Ethiopia, where holders of $1 billion in defaulted bonds began steps toward litigation after failing to agree on terms acceptable to both the investor group and official creditors co-led by China. Xuan also called for clearer rules identifying preferred creditors, after institutions in the Zambia and Ghana restructurings argued that their claims should be exempt from losses. The proposal does not change existing bond contracts, but it underscores the unresolved conflict between private enforcement rights, bilateral-creditor terms and the speed of sovereign workouts.

## China Adds an Overnight Tool as Regulators Challenge Inflated Ratings

The People’s Bank of China will conduct overnight reverse-repurchase operations on June 29 and June 30, adding a new tenor to a framework centered on the 7-day reverse repo rate. The change gives the central bank a direct instrument for managing overnight funding conditions and may eventually support a shift toward a policy benchmark closer to those used by other major central banks.

The existing 7-day rate is 1.4% and has been unchanged since May 2025. The new overnight operation will use a fixed rate, but the PBOC did not announce that rate in advance. Its level will determine whether the debut is primarily a liquidity-management change or carries an easing signal.

Standard Chartered’s Becky Liu said a rate of 1.25% or lower would amount to a de facto policy cut. Credit Agricole strategist Jeffrey Zhang expects 1.3%, near the level at which the interbank overnight repo rate normally trades, and anticipates that the PBOC will continue relying chiefly on 7-day operations while using the overnight facility to smooth seasonal funding pressure.

The transition is unlikely to be immediate. Most contracts used to hedge Chinese rate risk remain linked to the 7-day repo rate, which also anchors the current interest-rate corridor and the new repo facility for overseas central banks. Replacing it quickly would disrupt established pricing and hedging conventions.

Chinese government bonds nevertheless rallied modestly after the announcement, with the 10-year yield falling 1 basis point to 1.73%, its first decline in 5 sessions. The reaction reflected the possibility that an overnight benchmark could eventually deliver more precise control of bank funding or create another route for easing as growth loses momentum.

The PBOC is also pressing domestic rating companies to review the unusually large share of top-rated issuers in China’s bond market. Regulators have asked firms to reassess whether covered borrowers still meet updated AAA standards. One proposed indicator is the spread at issuance over comparable government debt; issuers paying more than 200 basis points could face a downgrade, though rating agencies would consider other factors.

At the end of the first quarter, 27% of more than 6,000 Chinese bond issuers carried AAA ratings and another 32% were rated AA+. By comparison, fewer than 1% of outstanding U.S. corporate bonds held a AAA rating from any of the three major international agencies. The concentration has limited the usefulness of ratings in distinguishing credit quality and persisted through years of corporate defaults.

A reduction in AAA designations could increase borrowing costs for weaker companies and widen differentiation in domestic credit. The number of affected issuers remains unclear, and the PBOC has not publicly specified a timetable. The initiative nonetheless represents a more concrete attempt to connect ratings with market pricing and default risk after cases in which distressed borrowers retained top domestic grades.

China is also testing offshore sovereign demand. The Ministry of Finance began marketing as much as €5 billion of euro-denominated bonds in 5-, 8- and 12-year maturities. Initial guidance was 15, 22 and 33 basis points over mid-swaps, respectively. The proposed sale comes only 7 months after a €4 billion issue attracted more than €100 billion of demand, much earlier in the year than China’s usual euro-market borrowing.

The timing takes advantage of receptive European markets before any further ECB tightening, but the outcome remains a pending transaction until final pricing and allocations are established. Its initial terms show China seeking diversified funding while the PBOC reshapes domestic money-market operations and regulators attempt to improve credit differentiation.

## Forward Market Significance

The first immediate test is the final University of Michigan consumer survey and the New York Fed’s Multivariate Core Trend Inflation measure at 10:00 ET on June 26. Michigan’s preliminary readings showed sentiment at 48.9, 1-year inflation expectations at 4.6% and longer-run expectations at 3.4%. Revisions will indicate whether the collapse in oil before Thursday’s shipping incident had begun to alter household expectations, while the New York Fed measure will test whether underlying inflation is consistent with Williams’s projected glide path.

Japan’s 3-month bill auction is expected around 12:35 JST on June 26, with an announced amount of about ¥4.1 trillion. The more important duration tests follow with roughly ¥2.8 trillion of 2-year JGBs on June 30 and ¥2.6 trillion of new 10-year bonds on July 2. Results will show whether weak demand at the 20-year sale was specific to fiscal and super-long-duration risk or reflects a broader reluctance to add JGB exposure after the BOJ’s increase.

Japan’s May labor, retail-sales and industrial-production data arrive on June 30, followed by the quarterly Tankan on July 1. The releases will test the BOJ’s view that AI-related exports and corporate pricing can offset some of the drag from energy imports. Strong investment plans or price expectations would reinforce Tamura’s call for regular increases; weaker domestic demand would support a slower path even if the bank still intends to normalize.

China’s official manufacturing, nonmanufacturing and composite purchasing-managers’ indexes are due June 30. The previous readings were 50.0, 50.1 and 50.5. They will provide the first broad June check on whether the slowdown that prompted calls for more stimulus is continuing as the PBOC introduces its overnight facility.

European inflation and labor data become the next test of reduced ECB-hike forecasts. Spain’s flash CPI and the European Commission’s business and consumer survey are due June 29. German unemployment and flash CPI follow June 30. The question is whether lower energy prices are arriving quickly enough to weaken broader inflation pressure, or whether Moulin’s concern about pass-through remains visible in national readings.

U.S. Treasury bill supply increases into quarter-end. Treasury will auction $92 billion of 13-week and $79 billion of 26-week bills on June 29 for July 2 settlement, followed by an $80 billion 6-week sale on June 30. The amounts are larger than the preceding comparable offerings. Demand and dealer allocations will test cash capacity across quarter-end without the support of another fixed-rate coupon auction.

The U.S. activity calendar then builds toward the holiday-shortened July 2 session. JOLTS vacancies and Conference Board consumer confidence arrive June 30, followed on July 1 by ADP employment, final manufacturing PMIs, the ISM manufacturing survey and construction spending. The prior ISM report showed manufacturing at 54.0 and prices at 82.1 but employment below 50, making the June composition important for the Fed’s balance between resilient output and persistent input costs.

June payrolls and weekly jobless claims are due at 08:30 ET on July 2. May payrolls increased 172,000, unemployment was 4.3% and average hourly earnings rose 0.3% on the month and 3.4% from a year earlier. Treasury’s 4- and 8-week bill auctions follow at 11:30, before the SIFMA-recommended 14:00 early close ahead of the July 3 holiday. The compressed schedule leaves less trading time to absorb a labor surprise, renewed Hormuz disruption or a weak auction result.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury curve steepens as softer PCE lowers real yields but Hormuz risk lifts inflation compensation
overall_summary.session_narrative:
May headline PCE rose 0.4%, below the 0.5% estimate, prompting a broad Treasury rally before persistent inflation and an afternoon oil reversal divided the close. The 2-year yield fell 2.4 basis points to 4.124% and the 5-year declined 1.1 basis points to 4.166%, while the 10-year was nearly unchanged at 4.394% and the 30-year rose 2.1 basis points to 4.862%. The 10-year real yield fell 2.1 basis points to 2.18%, but its breakeven rose 2.2 basis points to 2.214%.

The inflation relief remained qualified: annual headline inflation accelerated to 4.1%, core inflation reached 3.4%, and Kansas City Fed price gauges rose to their highest levels since 2022. A projectile strike on a vessel near the Strait of Hormuz then sent crude higher and restored energy-supply risk to the long end. The curve steepened even as a $44 billion 7-year auction cleared without a concession.

Japan supplied a separate duration warning as its 20-year bond auction drew the weakest demand since May 2025 amid uncertainty over future government borrowing and further BOJ normalization.
